Rotten Tomatoes | Letterboxd | Metacritic
Carolyn Jenkins is a voracious consumer of film and television. She graduated from Long Island University with an MFA in Screenwriting and Producing where she learned the art of character, plot, and structure. The best teacher is absorbing media and she spends her time reading about different worlds from teen angst to the universe of Stephen King.

Game of Thrones burned fast and bright for HBO, but as with all good things, it had to come to an end. The series ushered in a new era for television, creating a mainstream fantasy show that brought viewers in droves. The beginning years were the gold standard for narrative television, until they weren’t. The series also has one of the infamous finales of all time, earning an unfortunate black mark. The age of Game of Thrones has ended. Now it is the time of Narnia.

Greta Gerwig’s upcoming The Chronicles of Narnia adaptation could prove to be even bigger than HBO's brutal fantasy. The luster is gone from George R.R. Martin’s world of dragons and ice zombies while fans prepare for something new. Though it comes from a well-known property, this fantasy epic is going in another direction with its storytelling.

It isn’t any mystery why Game of Thrones fumbled its last few episodes – or even seasons. One of the biggest obstacles of the series was to translate George R.R. Martin’s words, even when the author had not finished the books. HBO creatives had presumed this would be accomplished by the time they caught up with the books, but every fantasy fan is familiar with how that story went.

blocks.c: Cast Placeholder Image

blocks.x: Chronicles of Narnia doesn’t have that problem. Writer C.S. Lewis created an ambitious and vivid world unlike any other in the 1950s. This story concluded with seven books that told a complete story. While previous feature film adaptations failed to tell the entire narrative in the mid-aughts, Greta Gerwig may have the secret sauce to correct that. The director isn’t adhering to the old standbys, either.

She is starting her franchise with the first chronological book, which isn’t The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, but The Magician’s Nephew. Before the Pevensies discover the magical wardrobe that takes them to Narnia, Narnia actually had to be created. This prequel story follows the adventures of two other children who discover the world of Charn. There they encounter Queen Jadis, who would go on to become the White Witch and spread evil throughout Narnia. The book also focuses on the mythical lion, Aslan, and his creation of Narnia.

Gerwig starting with the first chronological book is a logical step in the right direction. This way, she can control the output of the story, ensuring that it is told the right way. This sets the upcoming movie apart from previous adaptations and uses this potential to its benefit. Especially since the series is concluded, there will be no uncertainty in this rollout. It will just be a return to The Chronicles of Narnia.

blocks.x: The Magician’s Nephew is not only the perfect entry into the world of Narnia, but for some, may just be the perfect introduction to fantasy for the uninitiated. At the time of its release, Game of Thrones was refreshing because it was a more grounded version of The Lord of the Rings. Though there was some semblance of magic in Westeros, it was largely about the dark machinations of people. Viewers remember how that all ended, and it is high time that a colorful world of wonder and magic returns to the big screen.

A trailer for Greta Gerwig’s new film has already been released and shows exactly what fans can expect. The two children, Digory (David McKenna) and Polly (Beatrice Campbell), live in a drab world in England, and only when they enter the magician’s (Daniel Craig) workshop do they understand exactly what is possible. As the children discover the existence of other worlds, their awe will be matched by the audience's. This is the type of story that the visual medium is made for, and Gerwig has created exactly what viewers have needed all along.

If this is what fantasy fans can expect from the rest of the franchise, Netflix will have no problems getting people to tune in. In a rare show of support for theaters, the streamer will allow The Magician’s Nephew into theaters in February. This is exactly how this movie should be seen and should prove to be the beginning of something wonderful.

The Magician’s Nephew is not only the perfect entry into the world of Narnia, but for some, may just be the perfect introduction to fantasy for the uninitiated. At the time of its release, Game of Thrones was refreshing because it was a more grounded version of The Lord of the Rings. Though there was some semblance of magic in Westeros, it was largely about the dark machinations of people. If this is what fantasy fans can expect from the rest of the franchise, Netflix will have no problems getting people to tune in. In a rare show of support for theaters, the streamer will allow The Magician’s Nephew into theaters in February. This is exactly how this movie should be seen and should prove to be the beginning of something wonderful.
